home.line: Software engineer in Tokyo, focused on agentic coding and workflows for AI-generated content.

about.title: About
story: Born in Ho Chi Minh City. Landed in Minnesota on Valentine's Day 1998, age four, with my parents and sister. Grew up in Eagan and studied computer science and IT infrastructure at the University of Minnesota.

Before tech I did other work. A summer stamping metal at my dad's shop. A summer pulling crab cages with my uncle in the Louisiana bayous, 3am to 3pm in Gulf of Mexico heat. Years pulling espresso at Caribou Coffee and bartending through school. That work shaped how I think about craft: slow is fast, and the person next to you matters more than the tool in your hand.

My tech career started at Target in 2017. Then Zoom, Google, and now SmartNews in Tokyo, where I build the infrastructure behind AI-generated content and work out how teams can code well with agents. I live near Shibuya and I'm learning Mandarin.
recognition: Minnesota state champion, one-act play, forensics and speech

work.title: Work
work.intro: Nine years, four companies, one throughline: build for real people, and leave things better than I found them.

points: AI content infrastructure: LLM generation pipelines, editorial consoles, and delivery to web and native apps.
Designed review gates that combine agent and human moderation before AI-generated content publishes.
Led multi-model routing with request tracing and per-model cost attribution.
Ran 60+ product experiments, and drive evaluation and rollout of the engineering toolchain.
Components and layouts for Guided Support Experience and the Help Center.
Founding engineer on the Help Experience design system and its tokens.
Built the Zoom Events app and virtual events platform UI.
Re-architected CI/CD and introduced unit and integration testing.
Founding engineer on a global design system; mentored interns and new grads.
Performance and architecture for Target.com, from React-Redux to Next.js.
Helped launch Target's first design system.
Mentored engineers through the Technology Leadership Program.
